newsitem.title: USA: CALPERS ceases trading with Nomura.
newsitem.headline: CALPERS ceases trading with Nomura.

text.p: The California Public Employees' Retirement System (CalPERS) said on Monday that it would indefinitely stop all trading activity with Japan's Nomura Securities Co Ltd within the pension plan's internally and externally managed portfolios.
CalPERS also said it would remove the Japanese brokerage from the pension plan's list of approved securities lending firms.

On March 6, Nomura Securites revealed unauthorised trades by two of its managing directors who appeared to have funneled profits from the firm to a corporate account. It could not be confirmed whether the corporate account linked with a former "sokaiya" racketeer, as other media reports and CalPERS said.
The firm admitted on March 7 that it was highly likely the trades were illegal.
At present 14 external money managers contract with CalPERS and manage approximately $19.7 billion of its international equities and fixed income, the company said.
"We are deeply concerned with the events that have taken place at Nomura Securities," said Charles Valdes, chairman of CalPERS Investment Committee.
"As fiduciaries to one million members who belong to CalPERS, it is vital that we take the necessary actions to stop corporate blackmail."

CalPERS, the largest pension fund in the United States with $110 billion in assets, is not considering filing a lawsuit against Nomura Securities and said it does not intend to take action of any kind against Nomura Capital Management, which manages a $700 million portfolio.

Between July 1989 and February 1997, Nomura Capital Management's portfolio has returned a 5.2 percent annualised return versus the CalPERS Custom Pacific Basin Equity Benchmark return of a negative 1.4 percent.
